title: Post-Election Trends - Systematic Investor 321
speakers: Alan Dunne (Dublin-based co-host, macro/systematic investor; caption "alen Don")
summary: Top Traders Unplugged Systematic Investor 321 (Nov 2024, post US election): Alan Dunne and Niels on the Trump win (polls missed, inflation theme), the macro outlook (solid US growth, supply-side optimism, tariffs as bargaining chip, deficit/bond-yield risk), October's poor trend-following month (all three financial sectors reversed), a buffer-ETF question, Goldman's 3% 10-year S&P forecast and concentration, and the Invesco systematic investing survey.

coverage.note: Intro; European car industry and German government crisis
Europe competitiveness, demographics, policy paralysis; bearish on Europe; Don 50th anniversary
Election analysis: magnitude of win, polls underestimate, inflation theme, incumbents voted out
Niels thoughts: legal problems, inflation cause, podcasts, Musk, tariffs
Podcasts/Twitter, Musk, tariffs as bargaining chip, Bessent shadow Fed chair
US macro: recession risk faded, labour market, solid consumption, inflation, China policy
Asset market pattern, Trump policy expectations, tariffs one-off effect, supply-side optimism
Two years of control, deficit and bond yields rising since Fed cut, Bessent, deficit consensus
Own goal in yields, Fed pace revised, predictability, Greenspan-Clinton, deficits resolution; trend update intro
October trend-following loss: three financial sectors reversed, medium lookbacks, bond transitions
Trend index numbers; buffer ETF question and answer
Buffer ETFs vs trend, short duration; Goldman 10-year S&P forecast
Goldman concentration effect, forecasting swing variables, Alan view on yields and valuations
Discussion of concentration puzzle, rates and equities, trend followers do not predict, earnings vs valuations
Bond vs equity forecast, trend expected return, hard to sell alternatives; Invesco survey adoption stats
Invesco survey multi-asset systematic and AI usage; power of being systematic; mystery paper intro
Mystery paper: adding alternatives that trade held assets; outro

completeness_estimate: 0.75 - first reader caught the main arguments of each topic but skipped the secondary mechanisms and evidence (buffer ETF mechanics, Goldman forecast context and counter-arguments, Musk/podcast side topics, data-noise caveats, survey breadth).

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne (Dublin-based co-host, macro/systematic investor; caption "alen Don")
claims.quote: we've got this um challenge in Europe from the influx of EVS in particular from from from China
claims.claim: European autos (14 million jobs) face structural pressure from Chinese EV imports, shown by Volkswagen plant closure and pay-cut proposals.

claims.claim: The German coalition split over budget cuts reflects Europe's rising debt, flat growth and competitiveness challenges.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne (Dublin-based co-host, macro/systematic investor; caption "alen Don")
claims.quote: it's hard to make the uh the bullish case on Europe as far as I can see at the moment
claims.claim: Europe's bullish case is hard to make: policy paralysis, aging population, immigration reluctance and no tech leaders hurt productivity.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen (host; caption "Neil Castro blon")
claims.quote: all this EU bureaucracy that we have trying to always have 27 countries kind of agree on things
claims.claim: EU bureaucracy of 27 countries slows decisions and hurts competitiveness, so Europe is falling behind.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne (Dublin-based co-host, macro/systematic investor; caption "alen Don")
claims.quote: these Cycles are are long-term Cycles
claims.claim: Country relative economic strength moves in long cycles (Germany once far ahead, now Ireland has fiscal surpluses and full employment).

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne (Dublin-based co-host, macro/systematic investor; caption "alen Don")

claims.quote: High inflation and particularly grocery food prices that's really been the theme
claims.claim: High inflation (especially grocery prices) dominated the election even with full employment and record stocks.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne (Dublin-based co-host, macro/systematic investor; caption "alen Don")

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne (Dublin-based co-host, macro/systematic investor; caption "alen Don")

claims.quote: I think the interesting thing that that probably the market is jumping on is optimism around supply side policy
claims.claim: Markets are pricing optimism on supply-side policy (tax cuts, deregulation) that raises growth without inflation.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne (Dublin-based co-host, macro/systematic investor; caption "alen Don")
claims.quote: you basically have two years of cart blanch because you've got likely to have the the house and the senate for two years
claims.claim: Republicans control both houses and can use reconciliation for budget measures for two years, though moderates may limit spending and tax cuts.

claims.claim: The 10-year yield rose 60-70bp after the Fed's 50bp cut, reflecting deficit concerns.

correction.issue: Says 'equities held'. Niels said US equities did not lose much in October but other markets did, and calls the equity leg painful for trend followers as well, so equities were a third losing leg.
correction.fix: October 2024: fixed income peaked at the Fed cut and sold off, US equities lost little but other equity markets fell, and the dollar reversed to strength after being sold, so all three big financial sectors hurt trend followers together.
